subject: Staged uplift & instalment billing — proposal and options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@averyhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Staged uplift & instalment billing — proposal and options

Tom / Grace,

Following our call yesterday, attached is a concise SOW and a suggested commercial approach for the mid-contract uplift you mentioned (additional 40M tokens / month). The ask from Avery Procurement was clear: minimal invoice fragmentation but flexibility to scale in Q4. To balance those, we propose a staged instalment approach:

- Option A — One-time pro-rated invoice: invoice full uplift pro-rated to co-term date (single invoice in October).
- Option B — 3x instalments: split the uplift charge across 3 monthly invoices (Oct/Nov/Dec) with smoothing credit if usage lags.
- Option C — Escrow holdback: Avery prepays uplift to an escrow, Redwood draws down monthly against actual usage; unused funds are returned at co-term.

Each option includes a modest early-commit discount and a reconciliation true-up at co-term. I attached the updated SOW and the usage report you requested.

Please review and let us know which path procurement prefers — we can fast-track a DocuSign if they choose Option B or C.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Avery_Health_SOW_v3.pdf, usage_report_sep2026.csv
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@averyhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged uplift & instalment billing — proposal and options

Ben — thanks, got it. Procurement is nervous about multiple invoices across teams; they prefer single invoice per quarter. A couple of questions before we loop them in:

- If we go with Option B (3x instalments), can you provide a single consolidated invoice that shows the breakdown but is paid at once? Procurement insists on single payment flows but will accept internal allocations.
- For Option C (escrow), what is the proposed custodian and what's the SLA for refunds on unused amounts? Our legal team will want strong rollback language.

Also, our finance lead (procurement@averyhealth.com) wants to see the effect on ARR and whether any portion is refundable if usage drops. Can Grace or Lauren share the reconciliation cadence and sample invoice?

Tom
VP, Platform Engineering — Avery Health
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged uplift & instalment billing — proposal and options

Tom — really helpful questions, thank you. Quick answers and next steps below.

Consolidated billing (procurement-friendly):
- We can issue a single parent invoice for the quarter that lists the 3 instalment line items for accounting visibility while allowing your AP to make one payment. Internally we still record instalments for true-up logic.

Escrow specifics:
- Proposed custodian: BigBank Escrow Services (standard in our contracts).
- Refund SLA: unused escrow amounts returned within 15 business days after co-term reconciliation; we can tighten to 10 business days with a small fee credit.

Refundability and ARR impact:
- Instalments are billed as prepaid credits against usage; unused credits are refunded or converted into new credits at co-term per the SOW reconciliation. For ARR reporting, we can provide a schedule that separates consumed revenue vs deferred (we'll deliver a sample ledger export).

Action items I can take this afternoon:
1) Share a sample consolidated invoice and a templated escrow clause for legal.
2) Draft a one-page procurement summary comparing Option A/B/C and recommended default (we favor Option B for predictability + acceptance).
3) If you confirm procurement will accept a parent invoice with internal allocation, Ben and I will prep DocuSign for Option B with a small early-commit discount (1.5% of uplift) to expedite.

Can you confirm procurement contact (email) and whether they want the escrow custodian pre-approved? If so, I'll include BigBank contact details in the legal appendix.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Staged uplift & instalment billing — internal negotiation notes

Internal — forwarding thread with quick negotiation points before I send proc summary to Avery: 

- Approve consolidated parent invoice language (we can accept single AP payment while keeping instalment lines).
- I propose we offer Option B + 1.5% early-commit discount only if procurement signs within 7 business days.
- If procurement requests escrow, we accept BigBank but add a 10 business day refund SLA and a 25% fee waiver on reversal charges.
- If Procurement pushes for single non-refundable uplift that increases ARR recognition for them, escalate to finance for guidance.

Lauren / Ben — please confirm quickly so I can finalize the procurement one-pager.

Grace
(quoted attachments referenced above: Avery_Health_SOW_v3.pdf — SOW summary (3 pages); usage_report_sep2026.csv — last 6 months token usage)
